items.text: With one-line descriptions, Claude cannot tell that the three channels are alternatives rather than complements. Tool descriptions should say when to use each tool relative to the others, so stating each channel's use case and that exactly one channel is chosen per notification (C) fixes the cause. A system-prompt rule (A) is a weaker, global patch that leaves the tools themselves ambiguous. A PostToolUse hook (B) runs after a call has already executed, so it cannot cancel later calls; blocking a call is a PreToolUse job. Renaming the tools (D) groups them visually but still gives Claude no rule for choosing between them.
items.why: Erklaerung an neuen Distraktor anpassen, B korrekt begruenden, Verweis auf nicht vorhandene 'check preferences'-Option entfernen.

items.why: OS-Dateirechte erzwingen die Grenze ebenfalls (Stamm spricht sogar von 'infrastructure level'); neuer Distraktor: additionalDirectories erweitert den Zugriff, beschraenkt ihn nicht.

items.text: A pre-tool-call (PreToolUse) hook validates the target path before the Write or Edit runs and denies the call, so the modification never happens, and it works without touching the system prompt. A post-tool-call hook (C) fires only after the file was already changed. A system-prompt instruction (D) is probabilistic and can be overridden. `additionalDirectories` (B) grants Claude access to extra directories; it widens what can be reached and does not confine writes to the listed path.
items.why: Erklaerung an neuen Distraktor B anpassen.

items.text: A PostToolUse hook can replace the result Claude sees via `updatedToolOutput`, for MCP and built-in tools alike, so trimming each lookup to the 6 relevant fields stops the bloat before it accumulates over a multi-turn session. Adding a `fields` parameter (D) would be good tool design, but the server is third-party and cannot be changed. A system-prompt instruction to ignore fields (C) saves no tokens, because the fields are still in context. A larger context window (B) only postpones the problem and raises cost.
items.why: Erklaerung an eingegrenzten Stamm anpassen und updatedToolOutput (alle Tools) nennen.

items.text: `allowedTools` only auto-approves the tools it lists; it does not restrict Claude to them. Calls that need no approval run whether or not they are listed, and the Agent tool (formerly Task, which still works as an alias) is one of them, so leaving it out changes nothing (D). The thin single-agent response therefore has another cause, for example subagent descriptions too vague for Claude to delegate; clearer descriptions or naming the subagent in the prompt fix that. To actually stop spawning, put `Agent` in `disallowedTools`. A, B and C describe behaviors that don't exist.

items.text: A subagent's tool access is set by the `tools` field of its AgentDefinition: listing `["WebSearch"]` gives the subagent only that tool, while omitting the field inherits every tool available to subagents. `allowedTools` on the query only auto-approves the listed tools; it does not restrict which tools exist, so it cannot enforce least privilege. `tool_scope` and `tool_filter` are not AgentDefinition fields.
items.why: Erklaerung samt alter Correction-Notiz neu, passend zum neuen Schluessel.
